answer: Each identity seals an 8 GB replica of a public dataset, keyed to its own pubkey through a memory-hard encoding whose kernel takes 4 GPU-hours. Validators then issue random Merkle challenges with a 2 second deadline, so a hollow identity sharing one disk cannot answer fast enough. Failures slash a 20 token bond. For 10,000 clones the attacker needs 80 TB of NVMe (about $4,800), 40,000 GPU-hours (about $16,000), and 200,000 forfeited tokens if caught. Each replica is a mirror that only reflects one key, like a bank vault where every box needs its own physical steel.
